_comment: LV-087 — FROZEN BASELINE of the migration-ledger anomalies that already existed when the guard was written.
Two sections, two different defect classes: `duplicates` (same SQL applied under two filenames) and
`ledger_orphans` (a ledger row naming a migration that is not on disk / not in the other ledger).
Read by BOTH scripts/db-migrate.mjs (runtime refusal) and scripts/verify-migration-checksum-collision.mjs
(CI guard), so there is exactly one list and the two can never disagree.
WHY THESE ARE NOT FIXED RATHER THAN GRANDFATHERED: both files are already applied on the prod ledger
(_system._schema_migrations). Editing an applied migration breaks its checksum (never-edit-an-applied-
migration), and deleting one deletes ledger history to make a guard green — falsifying the audit trail.
Owner ruling 2026-08-05: do NOT retro-delete the existing duplicates; idempotency made the second run a
no-op. The guard exists to prevent the NEXT one.
Prod carries FOUR duplicate-checksum ledger pairs (876 applied rows / 872 distinct checksums). Only the
pair below still exists as two files on disk; for the other three the duplicate file was renumbered away
and survives in the ledger only, so there is nothing on disk for this guard to see:
Entries are pinned to the EXACT checksum AND the exact sorted filename list. A third file joining this
checksum, or any other pair, is NOT covered and fails. This baseline is append-only by review — adding an
entry means consciously accepting a duplicate, which is the decision the guard is meant to force.

duplicates.reason: Both applied on prod before LV-087. Idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS), so the second run was a no-op. Cannot be edited (applied checksum) or deleted (ledger history).

_ledger_orphans_comment: LEDGER ORPHANS — a row in ONE ledger with no counterpart, which the held registry does not explain.
The two ledgers are _system._schema_migrations (canonical, written by applyMigration) and
ih35_migrations.applied_migrations (mirror, also the ledger-backfill target for a hand-applied held
migration). Backend boot accepts a file that appears in EITHER, so a mirror row alone is enough to make a
migration look applied. That is the property being protected: a mirror row that nobody can tie to a real
file is a ledger that can lie in the direction of 'already done'.
Verified on prod br-fancy-credit-akjnd07a 2026-08-05 (current_user asserted in-statement):
canonical 876 rows, mirror 883, canonical-only 0, mirror-only 7. SIX of the seven are registered in
db/migrations/.held-migrations.json (the held union is held + applied_held + superseded = 171 files, NOT
just the 13 in `held`) and are therefore EXPECTED STATE — a held migration is hand-applied and
mirror-backfilled by design. Only the entry below is unexplained.
NOT DELETED, deliberately: removing a ledger row to make a guard green falsifies the migration audit
trail, which is the same rule that keeps the four duplicates above in place. It is recorded here instead so
it is explained rather than invisible.

ledger_orphans.reason: Mirror-ledger row for a migration with NO file in db/migrations/ and no canonical row. Its subject — re-casting the abandonment write to ::text — was itself a false premise: load_status_enum genuinely contains 'abandoned'/'driver_walkoff'/'driver_no_show' (added by 0094 via ALTER TYPE), so the cast was never needed and the file was dropped. Harmless operationally (db:migrate can never see a file that does not exist, so it cannot be re-applied), but it is a row asserting an application that cannot be evidenced. Recorded, not deleted.
